text:
samir: Heads-up — started a bulk restore job from prod snapshots in us-west1 and it's stalling on decrypts. Error: 'AccessDeniedException: Decrypt not allowed by key policy'. Anyone seen this pattern recently?
kelly: ugh. Was anything changed on KMS policies or the uploader role last night?
mike: We ran the RBAC prune at 02:10 UTC, but that should only affect service account bindings, not KMS grants. Still, possible the restore worker lost an attached role.
encops-bot: Alert: restore-job-9482 failed 42/120 objects: KMS Decrypt AccessDenied (aws:kms). Sample log: 
```
2026-03-23T02:33:14Z restore-worker-7 stderr: Failed to decrypt segment shard-1000: AccessDeniedException: Not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01
```
samir: That sample matches what we're seeing. Restore workers run under role `restore-worker@redwood-prod`. Can someone confirm the CMK key policy?
kelly: I checked key policy quickly — it has the usual account root + explicit grant for `restore-service-role`. But our runtime uses a different service principal since the infra migration (sts-assumed role). If the key policy used an `aws:PrincipalArn` exact match it could fail.
mike: Exact match would break on STS. We should prefer role ARN with wildcard or `aws:PrincipalOrgID` checks. For now we need a fast mitigation so restores can continue.
kelly: Agreed. Two options: 1) create a short-lived grant for the restore role, 2) rotate to an envelope key pattern and re-encrypt (slow). Option 1 is faster.
samir: If we do a grant, limit scope and TTL. Compliance will want audit logs.
compliance-ops: Please capture KMS audit events and the restore job IDs before any manual grants are created. We'll need the original failure evidence.
mike: I'll create a scoped temporary grant. Command I'm going to run (redacted ARNs):
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/prod-db-backups --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/restore-service-role --operations Decrypt --name temp-restore-grant-1767778000
```
mike: Creating now, will restrict via conditions and note TTL in the grant request metadata.
encops-bot: Action: created ticket ENCOPS-1234 (temp-kms-grant) assigned to mike.
mike: Grant created, verified via `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/prod-db-backups` (redacted output shows grant id G-0abc).
samir: Retrying the restore job now.
encops-bot: Restore job 9482 resumed: progress 60/120 -> 120/120, completed at 02:47 UTC. :tada:
kelly: Nice. We still need a permanent fix for the policy fragility and the RBAC prune interaction.
compliance-ops: Collected CloudTrail KMS events for the window 02:00-03:00 UTC. Please attach to ENCOPS-1234.
mike: Filed a follow-up engineering task (ENG-3642) to update key policies to allow STS-assumed role ARNs or use an IAM condition instead of exact principal matches. Also adding a pre-prune check to ensure service-account-role bindings used in key policies are in allowed list.
samir: I'll update the restore playbook: add a step to check KMS grant counts and a fallback to request temporary grant from EncOps with a standard template.
kelly: Add a note for oncall: when running RBAC prune, run `scripts/check-kms-binding.sh` and wait for confirmation from encops slack webhook.
mike: For the incident record: root cause = key policy principal mismatch post infra migration + RBAC prune removed binding used by restore workers; impact = delayed restore (~14m) on 1 bulk job; remediation = temporary grant granted; follow-ups = policy fix, pre-prune checks, playbook update.
compliance-ops: We'll mark this as "controlled exposure" and need the playback artifacts attached to the Jira before close.
samir: Thanks all. I'll draft the postmortem and ping legal/compliance for the formal review. Closing thread once ENCOPS-1234 and ENG-3642 have links.
kelly: thx, great coordination :thumbsup:
